editorial:
Imagine being a city kid from Beijing suddenly dropped into the middle of the giant Mongolian grasslands. That is exactly what happens to Chen Zhen, a student who wants to learn how to protect livestock from wolves. You get to see the world through his eyes as he meets the local nomads and discovers that nature is way more complex than any textbook. The vibe is very peaceful at first, but it quickly turns into a tense battle for survival. You will feel the wind and see the endless green hills, making the whole experience feel like a big trip to a place you have never been.

The animal scenes are the best part because the wolves feel like real characters with their own personalities. While the story moves a bit slow in the middle, the beautiful shots make up for it. You should definitely watch this if you love nature or stories about friendship between humans and animals.
endingExplained: The story ends on a sad note as the balance between humans and nature breaks. The government starts killing off the wolves to protect the sheep, which actually causes more problems because the remaining wolves become more aggressive. Chen Zhen realizes that trying to control nature with force is a mistake. He eventually leaves the grasslands, carrying the lessons he learned about respect and survival, while the old ways of the nomads fade away.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animal stories and beautiful scenery.
